justification: The package has Ce=0 (no outgoing dependencies) and Ca=1 (one incoming dependency), yielding stability I = 1.0. It does not depend on any other packages, so it cannot depend on less stable components. The only referenced package is com.google.gson.internal.bind (incoming, Ce=6, Ca=2), which depends on this util package rather than the util depending on it. Therefore Unstable Dependency is not present.

com.example has Ce=2, Ca=0 (instability I = 2/(2+0) = 1.0). Its outgoing dependencies: com.google.gson (Ce=5, Ca=12, I = 5/(5+12) = 0.294) and com.google.gson.reflect (Ce=1, Ca=9, I = 1/(1+9) = 0.100). Both outgoing packages have lower instability (are more stable) than com.example, so the Stable Dependencies Principle is respected and there is no Unstable Dependency smell.

The analyzed package has Ce=1 and Ca=0 => instability I = 1.0 (very unstable). Its only outgoing dependency is com.google.gson with Ce=5 and Ca=12 => instability I ≈ 0.294 (more stable). Since the package depends on a more stable package (I_dependent > I_dependency) and has no incoming dependencies, it does not violate the Stable Dependencies Principle; therefore Unstable Dependency is not detected.

com.google.gson.protobuf has Ce=1 and Ca=0 (stability I = 0/(0+1) = 0.0). Its sole outgoing dependency is com.google.gson which has Ce=5 and Ca=12 (stability I = 12/(12+5) ≈ 0.7059). Incoming dependencies to com.google.gson.protobuf = 0. Because the dependency (com.google.gson) is more stable than com.google.gson.protobuf, the Stable Dependencies Principle is respected and no Unstable Dependency smell is detected.
